findings.title: Unit mismatch: dollar prices passed to formatPrice, which expects cents
findings.detail: CartItem.price is documented as dollars (src/cart.ts). lineTotal and cartTotal return dollars. renderCart passes these values to formatPrice, which divides by 100 because it expects integer cents (src/money.ts). Input: one item { name: 'pen', price: 2, quantity: 3 } gives a line total of 6. renderCart prints 'pen x3: $0.06' and 'Total: $0.06' instead of $6.00. Every rendered cart shows totals 100 times too small. Fix: store price in cents in CartItem, or convert dollars to cents before the formatPrice call. Also consider integer cents to avoid float error in sums. The tests check only lineTotal and cartTotal and do not cover renderCart, so they do not catch this.

findings.title: No test for renderCart
findings.detail: The tests cover lineTotal and cartTotal only. Add a renderCart test that checks the formatted output. It would have found the unit mismatch.

findings.title: Cart passes dollar amounts to formatPrice, which expects integer cents
findings.detail: CartItem.price is documented as dollars. lineTotal and cartTotal return dollars. renderCart passes these values to formatPrice, and src/money.ts defines formatPrice as taking integer cents and dividing by 100. Example: one pen at price 2 (dollars) and quantity 3 gives a line total of 6. formatPrice(6) returns "$0.06" instead of "$6.00". Every rendered line and the Total are 100 times too small. The tests do not catch this because they cover only lineTotal and cartTotal, not renderCart. Fix: make CartItem.price integer cents, or convert dollars to cents (Math.round(x*100)) before the call to formatPrice. Add a renderCart test.

findings.title: Dollar floats in totals can give rounding errors
findings.detail: The cart sums floating-point dollar prices. For example, 0.1 + 0.2 gives 0.30000000000000004. Money values in this codebase are integer cents (see src/money.ts). Use integer cents for the price field to avoid this error and to fix the unit mismatch.

findings.title: Counter.increment loses updates under concurrent calls
findings.detail: The method reads the value with store.get, adds the amount, then writes with store.set. These are separate awaits, so there is no atomicity. The doc comment says many requests call increment at the same time. Example: the stored value is 0. Two calls run increment('a') together. Both read 0. Both write 1. The final value is 1, not 2. The KeyValueStore interface in src/store.ts has only get and set, so no atomic increment exists. Fix: add an atomic increment (for example incr or compare-and-set) to KeyValueStore and use it. Or serialize the calls per key. The test only calls increment one after another, so it does not detect this bug. Add a test that runs Promise.all of several increments and expects the sum.

findings.title: Counter.increment has a read-modify-write race that loses updates
findings.detail: increment() does get(), adds, then set() with an await between each step. The class doc says many requests call increment at the same time. Two calls on key 'a' with value 0 both read 0. One writes 1 and the other writes 1 (or 2). The final count is lower than the number of increments, so events are lost. The KeyValueStore interface in src/store.ts has only get and set, so no atomic operation exists. Fix: add an atomic increment (for example incrBy) to KeyValueStore, or a compare-and-set. Alternatively, serialize calls per key with a per-key promise queue. This only protects a single process.

findings.title: Test does not cover concurrent increments
findings.detail: The only test awaits each increment in sequence. It cannot detect the lost-update race. Add a test that runs Promise.all of several increments on one key against a store with an async delay, and expects the sum.

findings.title: Off-by-one in paginate slice start skips the first page of items
findings.detail: `start = current * pageSize` should be `(current - 1) * pageSize`. Pages start at 1. For 45 items, page 1, size 20, `start` is 20, so it returns items 20-39 and never returns items 0-19. For page 3 of 45 items, `start` is 60, so `items` is empty. The returned `page` and `pageSize` fields and `pageRange` use the correct 1-based formula, so the output is inconsistent: `pageRange` says '41-45 of 45' while `items` is empty. The test misses this because it checks only `totalPages` and `pageRange`, never `p.items`.

findings.title: Test does not assert the returned items
findings.detail: The 'describes the range' test checks `totalPages` and `pageRange` only. Add assertions on `p.items` for the first, a middle, and the last page. Add cases for an out-of-range page and an empty list. Such a test would have found the off-by-one bug.

findings.title: A NaN page is not clamped
findings.detail: `Math.min(Math.max(1, NaN), totalPages)` is NaN. The result has `page: NaN` and empty `items`. `clampPageSize` validates integers, but `page` has no validation at this boundary. Also, a non-integer page such as 1.5 gives a fractional slice start.

findings.title: paginate uses the wrong slice offset, so page 1 is skipped
findings.detail: In `paginate`, `start = current * pageSize` should be `(current - 1) * pageSize`, because pages start at 1. Input: 45 items, page 1, size 20. The code slices 20..40 and returns items 20-39 instead of 0-19. The last page returns an empty list: page 3 gives slice(60, 80) = []. `pageRange` computes the range with `(page-1)`, so the label disagrees with the items. The test never checks `p.items`, so it passes anyway.

findings.title: A NaN or non-integer page value is not handled

The docstring says an out-of-range page moves to the nearest valid page, but NaN and fractions are not handled. `clampPageSize` already validates integers, so apply the same check to `page`.

findings.title: Prefix check with startsWith allows escape to sibling directories
findings.detail: resolveUpload checks full.startsWith(UPLOAD_ROOT) without a path separator. UPLOAD_ROOT is /srv/app/uploads. Input '../uploads-private/secret.txt' resolves to /srv/app/uploads-private/secret.txt. That path starts with '/srv/app/uploads', so the check passes. readUpload then reads a file outside the upload directory. Any sibling directory whose name starts with 'uploads' is exposed. Fix: use path.relative and reject results that start with '..' or are absolute, or compare against UPLOAD_ROOT + path.sep. The same check also accepts the root itself (name '' or '.'), which readFile rejects as a directory. The test covers only '../etc/passwd', so it misses this case. Symlinks inside the upload directory are not resolved (no realpath) and can also escape.

That string starts with '/srv/app/uploads', so the check passes and readUpload reads a file outside the upload directory. This is a path traversal bypass for any sibling directory whose name begins with 'uploads'. Fix: compare with path.relative and reject results that start with '..' or are absolute, or test startsWith(UPLOAD_ROOT + path.sep). Also decide whether the root itself (name '' or '.') must be rejected, since it currently passes. The tests do not cover the sibling-prefix case. Symlinks inside the root are also not resolved (no realpath).

findings.title: Path containment check uses startsWith without a separator, so sibling directories escape it
findings.detail: resolveUpload checks full.startsWith(UPLOAD_ROOT), and UPLOAD_ROOT is '/srv/app/uploads' with no trailing separator. The input '../uploads-private/secret.txt' resolves to '/srv/app/uploads-private/secret.txt'. That string starts with '/srv/app/uploads', so the check passes. readUpload then reads a file outside the upload directory. Any sibling directory whose name starts with 'uploads' is exposed (for example 'uploads-old' or 'uploads_tmp'). The input '' or '.' also resolves to the root itself. Fix: use path.relative(UPLOAD_ROOT, full) and reject a result that starts with '..' or is absolute. Alternatively, check full === UPLOAD_ROOT || full.startsWith(UPLOAD_ROOT + path.sep). Symlinks inside the directory are also not resolved. Use realpath if users can create links. The test only covers '../etc/passwd', so it does not catch this case. Add a test for '../uploads-evil/x'.

findings.title: Path traversal: startsWith check lets sibling directories pass

With UPLOAD_ROOT=/srv/app/uploads, the input `../uploads-private/secret.txt` resolves to /srv/app/uploads-private/secret.txt. That path starts with the root string, so no error is thrown. `readUpload` then reads a file outside the upload directory. An absolute name such as `/srv/app/uploads2/x` fails the same way. Fix: compare with `full === UPLOAD_ROOT || full.startsWith(UPLOAD_ROOT + path.sep)`, or use `path.relative` and reject results that start with `..` or are absolute. Symlinks inside the root are also not resolved. Use `realpath` if users can create links.

findings.title: Global regex with .test() keeps lastIndex, so consecutive secret lines are missed
findings.detail: SECRET_PATTERN uses the /g flag and is shared at module level. RegExp.test() on a /g regex starts at lastIndex and sets lastIndex after a match. Input 'password: x\npassword: y' gives: line 1 matches and sets lastIndex to 9. Line 2 is then searched from index 9, finds no match, and resets lastIndex to 0. findSecretLines returns [1] instead of [1,2]. A secret detector then silently misses real secrets, and results depend on call history. Fix: remove the g flag, or create the regex inside the function. The test has only one secret line, so it does not catch this.

Line 2 is then searched from index 9, finds no match, returns false, and resets lastIndex. findSecretLines returns [1] and not [1,2]. A secret scanner then reports a false negative. Remove the g flag, or set lastIndex = 0 before each test. The single test has only one secret line, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: parseId now throws, but getUser still checks for null
findings.detail: The diff changes parseId to throw a RangeError instead of returning null. The only other caller, getUser in src/handler.ts, was not updated. It still tests `id === null` and returns a 400 'bad id' reply. Input: getUser('abc') or getUser('0'). Before the change, the reply was {status:400, body:'bad id'}.
